Why Apple Silicon

Traditional GPU inference requires fitting the entire model in VRAM. A 16 GB consumer GPU cannot run a Q4-quantized 13B model — it doesn't fit. Your options were an expensive workstation GPU or a cloud API.

Apple Silicon's unified memory means GPU and CPU share one pool. A 16 GB Mac mini loads a Q4 8B model (~5 GB) with room for the OS and other apps. No VRAM ceiling.

Every model listed here is open-weight: publicly released weights, no API keys, no telemetry, no vendor agreement. The weights you download today run the same way in five years — fully air-gapped if needed.

The real cost question

The financial argument for local isn't API cost savings. At $0.01 per document interaction with cloud models, token savings don't recoup hardware for years.

The real cost is compliance overhead: the vendor due diligence, the BAA negotiations, the conversation with your malpractice carrier about your AI vendor's breach notification process. A local machine eliminates most of that — not by being cheaper per token, but by removing the third-party processor from the compliance equation entirely.

The hardware also has a 4–6 year useful life and does everything else a laptop or desktop does. It's infrastructure, not a pure AI line item.
